sources.RFC 9001 (rfc-editor.org text, sha256 3b: section 5: Retry packets use AEAD_AES_128_GCM; Initial packets use AEAD_AES_128_GCM with keys derived from the Destination Connection ID of the client's first Initial; all other packets use keys and algorithms negotiated by TLS. 5.1: separate secrets for each direction at every encryption level. 5.4.3: AEAD_AES_256_GCM's header protection is AES-256. 4.8: a TLS alert becomes CRYPTO_ERROR 0x0100 + AlertDescription. 4.6: 0-RTT. 7: Initial packets are not protected with a secret key.
sources.RFC 8446 (rfc-editor.org text, sha256 47: 4.1.3: the single cipher suite the server selects; 7.3: [sender]_write_key, a key per sending side; 4.1.1: no overlap aborts with handshake_failure or insufficient_security; 9.1: MUST implement TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, SHOULD implement TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256; 2: ClientHello and ServerHello precede every protected message.

alternatives.keep the node provider: refused by the directive: ChaCha20-Poly1305 negotiated with a peer that offers it alone or first (01-red-base-providers.log)
alternatives.narrow the daemon's side only: a shards client would still offer ChaCha20-Poly1305 to a server that prefers it; the tests hold both directions (either_way)
alternatives.one provider object for the QUIC links a: not possible without changing a TLS stack: crates/remote builds on hyper-tls (hyper_quic::rustls), crates/server on crates.io rustls 0.23, distinct CryptoProvider types; sharing would put hyper-tls into the guest server binary, which every microVM's server device carries (TLS's guest cost measured in PM M122). So: one provider for every QUIC link (tls::provider, used by server, owner_server, client, client_with) and one for the in-VM server (prepare, used by its ServerConfig and client verifier)
alternatives.a suite constant in shards-abi that each: not taken: an indirection for one constant whose effect each side's tests pin by the negotiated suite (R05, R13)
alternatives.also narrow the key exchange groups, as: not taken: the directive is the AEAD; the node groups are hybrid post-quantum only and unchanged

decision.compatibility: Between shards builds nothing changes: an earlier shards offered AES-256-GCM first and daemons follow the client's order, so every pair of builds negotiates AES-256-GCM (an_earlier_shards_still_connects_on_aes_256_gcm; every_link_is_aes_256_gcm_at_both_ends is green on the base too). Refused now: a peer offering no AES-256-GCM, e.g. one implementing only RFC 8446 section 9.1's mandatory AES-128-GCM. A peer preferring another suite but offering AES-256-GCM (Go's crypto/tls either way) gets AES-256-GCM.
decision.literals: none new in production beyond the suite the directive names; test fixtures: 16 delivery rounds in each in-memory exchange, as the existing handshake harness had
